justifications.c1: Independent trade sources give £15-£30/t per rejected load (FW column £15.25/t; Glencore adviser £20/t; AHDB via Farming News £20-£30/t, search-confirmed), i.e. roughly £450-£870 per load; the idea's £2k-£10k per load was not supported; sector £20m figure is a merchant claim.
justifications.c2: AHDB says check temperature every few days then weekly, insects weekly until 5°C; Red Tractor assessors expect weekly post-harvest monitoring records; Soil Association weekly; a mandated weekly task during each storage season (seasonal, then monthly).
justifications.c3: Manual probing routine documented by AHDB with probe hardware prices (£104.50-£285 ex VAT, SW Seeds) and Red Tractor paper template; labour time per probing round not quantified.
justifications.c4: Red Tractor storage standard (search-confirmed) requires records of temperature, moisture, dates of checks and follow-up, investigation of temperature rises and annual probe calibration; enforcement evidence is thin (NC document and 'unassured grain claims rebuffed' not seen).
justifications.c5: Farm owner/manager pays rejection charges (FW column) and already buys £3k-£4.8k store-monitoring systems (Barn Owl testimonial); fragmented but owner-operators hold the budget; no job-advert evidence.
justifications.c6: Frontier/Javelot monitoring is for merchants' own stores (extension to growers not confirmed); Dealey store-hygiene contractors visit but no evidence they sell monitoring; equipment sold via shows/dealers.
justifications.c7: Crowded UK field: Martin Lishman Barn Owl and AgroLog, Robydome StoreCheck, Farmex, Javelot, OPI, Onsenso; paying customers exist but researcher states no source shows which gap is unmet.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN temperature transmitters £74-£175 (Innon) with multi-year battery (vendor), Milesight TS101 insertion sensor for grain stacks; Purdue notes hot spots need dense sensors, raising per-store cost.
justifications.c9: Red Tractor annual record and calibration cycle plus comparable fees (Barn Owl £525/yr after year one; AgroLog £180/device/yr) from one FW roundup whose prices could not be search-confirmed.
justifications.c10: Repeated Farmers Weekly coverage of insect rejections, NFU rejections hub, Scottish FAS advice; researcher searched for and found no farmer-forum threads and no regulator enforcement data.

weakest: A rejected load costs only about £450-£870, and the UK already has several wireless grain-spear products with subscriptions, leaving no evidenced gap.
